extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent practitioners, patent owners/agents
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and criteria for determining patent term, eligibility for patent term adjustment (PTA) under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and related regulations, and patent term extension (PTE) under 35 U.S.C. 156, including procedures, limits, and duties (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent term (20-year term) calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to fee payment, patent term begins on the date the patent issues and ends 20 years from the date on which the application for the patent was filed in the United States or, if the application contains a specific reference to an earlier-filed application under sections 120, 121, 365(c), or 386(c), from the date on which the earliest such application was filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents are treated differently (see MPEP §1505); amendments from the Hague Agreement and Patent Law Treaties Implementation Act affect cited sections (e.g., insertion of 386(c)). Continuations, internationals entering national stage, and continuing applications' term endpoints are governed by the earliest priority/benefit-claim as specified; foreign priority under 119/365/386 is not considered in determining the 20-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-URAA/continuation 17-year-from-grant rule and comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: For patents in force on or resulting from applications filed before the date 6 months after enactment of the Uruguay Round Agreements Act, the patent term is the greater of the 20-year term or 17 years from grant (subject to terminal disclaimers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects patents filed before June 8, 1995. Remedies (sections 283, 284, 285) limited for acts commenced before the URAA date. When comparing expiration dates for patents with terminal disclaimers, care must be taken because printed dates on the patent face may be incorrect due to statutory changes; Certificate of Correction under 37 CFR 1.323 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign priority and domestic provisional benefit not counted toward term
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign priority under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d), 365(a), 365(b), 386(a), or 386(b), and domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) to U.S. provisional applications are not considered in calculating the twenty-year term.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application claiming such benefits ends twenty years from the U.S. filing date (or earliest effective U.S. benefit date under 120/121/365(c)/386(c)), not from the foreign/international filing or provisional filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining expiration date when a terminal disclaimer is present
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine the original expiration date of a patent subject to a terminal disclaimer, examine the terminal disclaimer language in the patent file history; if it disclaims the terminal portion beyond the expiration of an earlier patent, the earlier patent's expiration may control unless a specific date was provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the printed terminal disclaimer date on the patent face is incorrect due to statutory changes, request Certificate of Correction (37 CFR 1.323). Patent term extension under 35 U.S.C. 156 may still apply to patents subject to terminal disclaimers, but PTA under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) cannot extend beyond the disclaimer-specified date (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(B) and 37 CFR 1.703(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing-date-based eligibility for PTA/PTE
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for patent term extension/adjustment depends on application filing dates: applications filed between June 8, 1995 and May 28, 2000 are governed by former 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.701; applications filed on or after May 29, 2000 are governed by 35 U.S.C. 154(b) as amended and 37 CFR 1.702–1.705.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design patents are not eligible for PTA. Patents issuing from applications filed before June 8, 1995 are not eligible for PTA under 35 U.S.C. 154, but may be eligible for PTE under 35 U.S.C. 156.

rubrics_metrics.name: Former 35 U.S.C. 154(b) grounds for extension (interference/secrecy/appellate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under former law (applicable to certain filing dates), a patent may be extended if issuance was delayed due to interference/derivation proceedings, secrecy orders, or appellate review reversing an adverse determination; total extensions under that subsection cannot exceed five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions for appellate review are limited if the patent is subject to a terminal disclaimer. Periods of extension are reduced by time attributable to appellate review within three years of filing and by applicant failure to act with due diligence as determined by the Commissioner. Examiners do not make extension decisions under 37 CFR 1.701; any extension granted is printed on the patent face.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTA grounds: failure to perform specified PTO actions within statutory timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) and 37 CFR 1.702, a patent term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to the Office's failure to: (i) mail required notifications or a notice of allowance within specified months (14-month/14-month/earlier/4-month distinctions depend on effective dates), (ii) respond to a reply or appeal within 4 months, (iii) act within 4 months after certain Board or court decisions where allowable claims remain, or (iv) issue a patent within 4 months after issue fee paid and requirements satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of multiple regulatory effective dates (e.g., changes effective January 14, 2013 and April 1, 2013), the exact measurement (14-month vs 4-month accounting/when measured) depends on grant/filing and notice dates; examiners must determine which regulatory version applies for a given application/patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year pendency adjustment (PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to the Office's failure to issue a patent within three years after the actual filing date (or date national stage commenced for internationals), subject to exclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclusions from the 3-year pendency calculation include time consumed by continued examination requested by applicant (132(b)), interference/derivation proceedings, secrecy orders, review by PTAB or Federal courts, and delay requested by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by interference/derivation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed due to interference or derivation proceedings under 35 U.S.C. 135(a), measured as the days the application was involved or suspended due to such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.702(c) was amended to reflect statutory replacement of interference with derivation proceedings for some applications; measurement includes days from institution to termination and periods of suspension caused by other interferences not involving the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by secrecy orders
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed because the application was under a secrecy order under 35 U.S.C. 181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure days maintained in sealed condition, time from mailing examiner’s answer under secrecy order to removal of order, and related notification/mailing intervals described in 37 CFR 1.701(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays caused by successful appellate review
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent term shall be adjusted if issuance was delayed by appellate review by the Patent Trial and Appeal Board or by a Federal court where the patent was issued pursuant to a decision reversing an adverse determination of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A remand by a PTAB panel can be considered a decision reversing an adverse determination for P T A purposes if it is the last panel action prior to a notice of allowance and no RCE was filed without intervening action/notice of allowance. Periods of appellate review are subject to reduction for review time occurring within three years of filing and for periods where applicant failed to act with due diligence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: overlapping delay periods not double-counted
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent periods of delay attributable to multiple statutory grounds overlap, the period of any adjustment granted shall not exceed the actual number of days the issuance of the patent was delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.701(b) / 35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(A) require careful computation to avoid double-counting overlapping delay categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation: terminal disclaimer caps PTA
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent whose term has been disclaimed beyond a specified date may be adjusted under 35 U.S.C. 154(b) beyond the expiration date specified in the disclaimer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if statutory PTA would otherwise extend term, the terminal disclaimer's specified expiration controls for PTA purposes (35 U.S.C. 154(b)(2)(B); see MPEP §2701 guidance re: Certificate of Correction and PTE interactions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of adjustment for applicant delay / failure to engage in reasonable efforts
rubrics_metrics.description: The period of adjustment shall be reduced by periods during which the applicant failed to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution; for PTA under paragraph (1)(B), cumulative periods in excess of 3 months taken to respond to an Office notice are deemed failure to engage unless restored under due care rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement counts time from date notice was given/mailed. The Director shall prescribe regulations defining circumstances constituting failure to engage in reasonable efforts. The Director may reinstate up to three additional months per response upon a due care showing made before issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for determination of PTA (notice, reconsideration, and reinstatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director shall prescribe procedures for applying for and determining patent term adjustments, must make a determination and transmit notice no later than the date of issuance, provide one opportunity to request reconsideration, and may reinstate all or part of cumulative periods upon a due care showing (no more than three additional months per response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director shall proceed to grant the patent after completion of the Director's determination regardless of any appeal taken by the applicant of that determination; if applicant dissatisfied with reconsideration decision, exclusive remedy is civil action in EDVA within 180 days after Director's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal limits and remedies for PTA determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant dissatisfied with the Director's decision on reconsideration has the exclusive remedy of a civil action against the Director in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia within 180 days; chapter 7 of title 5 (APA) applies. PTA determinations cannot be appealed or challenged by third parties prior to grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any final judgment changing the adjustment period must be served on the Director who will alter the patent term accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory/effective date complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple versions of 37 CFR 1.702–1.705 and related provisions exist due to various statutory and regulatory effective dates (e.g., changes effective April 1, 2013; January 14, 2013; September 16, 2012), and different versions apply depending on application and patent dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office personnel must carefully consider effective-date provisions to determine the correct version of the regulation to apply to a particular application or patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure and candor in Patent Term Extension (PTE) proceedings (37 CFR 1.765)
rubrics_metrics.description: A duty of candor and good faith toward the USPTO, the Secretary of HHS, and the Secretary of Agriculture rests on the patent owner/agent and on every individual substantively involved in a PTE proceeding; those aware of material adverse information must bring it to the attention of the Office or Secretary as soon as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is 'material' when there is a substantial likelihood the Office or Secretary would consider it important in determinations in the PTE proceeding. Disclosures should accompany copies of written documents and may be submitted via the USPTO electronic filing system using designated document descriptions/codes (e.g., 'Disclosure Under 37 CFR 1.765 in a Patent Term Extension Application').

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for fraud or material nondisclosure in PTE proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent will be determined eligible for extension, and no extension will be issued, if fraud on the Office or Secretary was practiced or attempted or the duty of disclosure was violated through bad faith or gross negligence; such determinations are made under §1.750 and require clear and convincing evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because PTE eligibility determinations may be made solely on representations in the PTE application, final determinations refusing PTE for fraud or duty violations are expected to be rare. See MPEP §2010 for related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation of third-party participation in PTE proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions on behalf of third parties (protests or otherwise) will not be considered in PTE proceedings and will be returned or otherwise disposed of without consideration; 37 CFR 1.765(d) precludes third-party submissions to the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTE proceedings before the Office are ex parte matters between the patent owner/agent and the Office; absent an invitation from the Director, third-party filings are inappropriate (In re Dubno, 12 USPQ2d 1153).

rubrics_metrics.name: Express withdrawal of application for extension
rubrics_metrics.description: An application for extension of patent term may be expressly withdrawn before a determination is made by filing a written declaration of withdrawal signed by the owner of record or agent; withdrawal is effective when acknowledged in writing by the Office and does not entitle applicant to refund of filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for withdrawal after the date permitted for reply to the final determination must be submitted on or before that date and accompanied by a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee. Withdrawal in other contexts (e.g., in response to an election requirement) has special considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for stay in processing of PTE application
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.182 may be filed to stay processing of a PTE application when unresolved issues relating to the patent remain; any such petition can be granted only for up to six months and requires showing of good and sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the patent term under 35 U.S.C. 154(a) and (b) has lapsed or will lapse during the requested stay, the patent owner must show that justice requires the stay and provide detailed reasons. Examples of granted and denied petitions are provided in MPEP (e.g., U.S. Patent No. 8,829,165 granted; contrast U.S. Patent No. 5,196,404 denied-in-part).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing of PTE applications when a reissue is filed
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent for which extension has been sought is reissued during PTE application processing, the original patent no longer exists; notice of the reissue should be provided and documents transferred to the reissue patent file rather than filing a new PTE application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.182 should be filed in the original patent to request transfer of the PTE application and associated documents to the reissue patent file, including updated information reflecting claim scope changes. For calculating extension to which the reissued patent is entitled, the original patent grant date is used so long as the reissued patent claims the approved product.
